name: Sheniu (社牛)
blurb: Chinese slang for a fearless socializer who is never embarrassed in public
title: Sheniu (社牛) Meaning: Chinese Slang for a Fearless Socializer
description: 社牛 (shèniú) is a fearless socializer who chats with strangers and never feels awkward. The opposite of 社恐, popular since 2021. With 社恐 and 社死.
answer: 社牛 (shèniú) describes someone with zero social pressure: they talk to strangers, let loose in public and do not care what anyone thinks. It is short for 社交牛X症, a joking "syndrome" whose middle part is a crude word for "awesome", and it is the opposite of 社恐 (shèkǒng, social anxiety). The word spread in summer 2021 with a wave of short videos; at first it was a tease, now it is mostly admiring.

body: In 2021, Chinese users started calling people in viral short videos, who shouted greetings in public and did outrageous things without a hint of embarrassment, cases of 社交牛X症. An article on People's Tribune (人民论坛网) traces the trend to an early internet personality who had posted public-prank videos since 2006 and went viral again in 2021; another account says the word first appeared in a Bilibili comment in July 2021. The exact origin is unclear.

Because the full form contains a vulgar word, media and polite conversation use the short form 社牛. A Pengpai (The Paper) piece from September 2021 notes that the word moved from slightly negative to positive.

sections.h: 社牛, 社恐 and 社死

head: Term
Full form
Meaning
rows: afraid of or avoiding socializing; online it is usually self-mockery, not a diagnosis
a public embarrassment so bad you want to vanish

body: The three often appear together: a 社恐 person dreads 社死, while a 社牛 person never seems to suffer it, or does not care.

ul: 「他入职第一天就记住了全组人的奶茶口味，社牛本牛。」 (First day on the job and he knew everyone's bubble tea order. A true sheniu.)
「我朋友是社牛，在地铁上都能和陌生人聊起来。」 (My friend is a sheniu; she chats with strangers on the subway.)
「社恐的我，年会上被迫当了一回社牛。」 (Shy me was forced to be a sheniu at the company party.)
「社牛也有翻车的时候，一不小心就社死。」 (Even a sheniu can crash and burn into total embarrassment.)

body: Calling someone 社牛 is usually friendly and a little impressed. But forcing "sheniu" behavior where others are uncomfortable, such as over-the-line jokes with strangers or being loud in public, is not social skill; it is just bothering people. Avoid the uncensored full form in polite company.

faq.a: Today it is mostly positive or neutral, meaning outgoing and unselfconscious. When it first spread it teased people who did over-the-top things without feeling embarrassed.

faq.q: What is the opposite of 社牛?
faq.a: 社恐 (shèkǒng), social fear or anxiety. A third related word is 社死 (shèsǐ), "social death", a humiliating public moment.

faq.q: Does saying 社恐 mean someone has social anxiety disorder?
faq.a: Not necessarily. As a People's Tribune article points out, social phobia is strictly a medical term, while most people who call themselves 社恐 online have no diagnosis and are describing social fatigue or nerves.
